sources.entry: BitMatch - Offloads camera cards to several drives and verifies every copy with SHA-256 before the card is erased.

summary.one_liner: BitMatch is a free, open-source macOS app that copies camera cards to several drives and verifies the copies with checksums so you know when a card is safe to erase.
keywords: free alternative to paid offload software
summary.what_it_does: BitMatch copies files from a camera card to one or more destination drives in a single pass, reading the card once and writing to every drive at the same time. In its default Standard mode it hashes new files as they copy and reads each drive back with SHA-256; reused files get a fresh source read. Thorough mode also rereads the card, and Paranoid additionally compares bytes, while Quick only checks sizes and never earns a safe verdict. It tracks each card as a queue row with its own progress and verdict, and supports one-time or multi-card project transfers. It can also compare two folders or check a backup against saved checksums, including ASC MHL and MHL 1.1 inventories, and it exports PDF, CSV, and JSON reports. The README says it skips recognized AppleDouble "._" files by default and does not mark a card safe to erase when files are excluded or when two folders share one physical drive.
use_cases: offload camera cards to backup drives
verify footage copies before formatting a card
make a second independent backup of shoot footage
generate checksum manifests to hand over with deliveries
compare two folders or check a backup against saved checksums
produce copy reports for producers or clients
how_to_run: Or download the signed and notarized macOS build from the Releases page
stack: Swift and Xcode (implied by Mac and iPad schemes)
notable: Standard mode hashes files while copying and reads each destination back with SHA-256 before giving a safe-to-erase verdict
Explicit verdict logic: Quick never earns safe to erase, and online-only iCloud/Dropbox files or changing sources do not either
Two folders on the same physical drive count as one backup
ASC MHL inventories for handing over checked backups
Built-in diagnostics export that omits footage names and paths
caveats: README calls it beta software from a one-person project and says not every camera, drive, filesystem, hub, or OS combination has been tested
Requires macOS 15.5 or newer; iPad and iPhone need iPadOS/iOS 18.5 or newer and must be built from source for now
Optional SFTP backup is listed as Mac-only
Licence terms restrict using the name and charging for essentially the same app on the App Store
summary.license: MIT (with additional request in README not to rebrand or sell near-identical forks; see LICENSE and BRANDING.md)
